name: Santan Expansion Lateral

values.StartLocation: El Paso South System Line 2000 interconnect

researcher_notes: Not in the sheet: no row for Santan, Salt River Project, Gilbert or Coolidge, and no Arizona row matches. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects workbook dated August 2026, sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 332, lists the Santan Expansion Lateral as completed in August 2004, intrastate, Arizona, 36 miles, 24 inch, 200 MMcf/d added, sponsor listed as SRG (Saltriver Group) Inc. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2006 says the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (docket CP06-57) approved El Paso Natural Gas buying a 37 mile lateral from the Salt River Project for about $32 million. The article gives 342,500 Dth/d capacity, joins El Paso South System Line 2000, and ends at the Santan plant in Gilbert. Salt River Project held repurchase options that could pass part of the capacity to Transwestern. An archaeological survey record at the Digital Archaeological Record names a 36 mile Santan Expansion pipeline from Gilbert to Coolidge. Length is staged as 36 mi from the Energy Information Administration; the article says 37. Capacity is staged from the article in Dth/d; the Energy Information Administration figure of 200 MMcf/d differs. Current owner is not confirmed: El Paso Natural Gas is staged as the 2006 buyer, and whether Transwestern exercised its options was not found. Owner name has no exact match in the ownership gazetteer, so it is recorded as the source spells it, and a legal form was not found. Salt River Project does have an exact gazetteer match (E100000001291) if the original owner is wanted instead. Passes the length rule (36 mi is over 15.5 mi) and is operating, so it is added as a record of an existing line. No route was found. Intrastate line, so absence from Federal Energy Regulatory Commission pipeline lists is not a concern. Confidence medium: three sources of different origin, but a conflict on capacity, length and owner.
